title: Annotatio IV §.XXII: Torun Confession — earthly natural; heavenly SPIRITUAL MYSTICAL CELESTIAL; simultaneous exhibition
pass_a_gloss: It may seem not alien from our Theological office to have brought into the midst our Marchic Church’s Symbolic Torun Confession on the Lord’s Supper… than which we have seen none concerning the Supper more excellent and fuller: It is clear therefore, say the Torun men, that this Sacrament consists of earthly things, bread and wine, and heavenly, the Lord’s body and blood, which though in a diverse mode are yet both most truly, most really, and most presentingly exhibited to us; namely, the Earthly in a natural, corporal and earthly mode; but the Heavenly in a SPIRITUAL, MYSTICAL AND HEAVENLY MODE, which inscrutable to Reason and sense we hold by Faith alone… Hence also the earthly Thing, Bread and Wine, truly are and are called Christ’s very body and blood, not indeed Substantially or CORPORALLY, but SACRAMENTALLY and MYSTICALLY, or through and on account of the Sacramental union, which consists not in bare Signification, nor only in Sealing, but also in THAT JOINED AND SIMULTANEOUS EXHIBITION AND COMMUNICATION OF THE EARTHLY AND HEAVENLY THING, though diverse in mode.
pass_b_english: Torun Confession (Marchic symbolic): the Sacrament is earthly bread and wine plus heavenly body and blood — both most truly and really exhibited, but in diverse modes.

Earthly: natural/corporal; heavenly: SPIRITUAL, MYSTICAL, HEAVENLY mode held by faith alone. Bread and wine are called body and blood sacramentally and mystically — not substantially/corporally — by a joined simultaneous exhibition of earthly and heavenly, not bare signification or sealing only.
source_text: A munere nostro Theologico haud alienum videri potest, Ecclesiæ nostræ Marchicæ Symbolicam Confessionem Toruniensem de Cœna Domini… adduxisse in medium, quâ nullam de Cœna vidimus excellentiorem plenioremque: Constat igitur, inquiunt Torunienses, hoc Sacramentum rebus terrenis, pane & vino, & cælestibus, corpore & sanguine Domini, quæ diverso quidem modo, utraque tamen verissimè, realissimè, ac præsentissimè nobis exhibentur; nempe, Terrena, modo naturali, corporali & terreno; Cælestes verò MODO SPIRITUALI, MYSTICO ET CŒLESTI, quem Rationi & sensui inscrutabilem sola Fide tenemus… Hinc etiam Res terrena, Panis & Vinum, verè sunt & dicuntur ipsum corpus & sanguis Christi, nonquidem Substantialiter, aut CORPORALITER, sed SACRAMENTALITER & MYSTICE, seu, per & propter unionem Sacramentalem, quæ non consistit in nuda Significatione, neque tantùm in Obsignatione, sed etiam in CONJUNCTA ILLA ET SIMULTANEA REI TERRENE ET CŒLESTIS, quamvis diversimoda, EXHIBITIONE ET COMMUNICATIONE.
